sections.html: Effingham sits on the northwest side of metro Savannah. Springfield holds the courthouse, Rincon is the biggest town, and Guyton is the third city. The county counted 64,769 people in 2020 and is estimated at 74,397 as of July 2025, with 212 building permits issued in 2025. Median home value is $276,000, and roughly 78 of every 100 homes are lived in by their owners. Steady growth means buyers are active, and equity tends to build, which makes a clean tax record worth protecting before you list.

sections.h2: Who values your property and who bills it?
sections.html:
Two offices split the work. The Board of Tax Assessors puts a value on each parcel. The Tax Commissioner turns that value into a bill and collects it, and says plainly that it sets neither values nor millage. Rates come from the Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education.

sections.h2: The 2026 bill and the county's tax relief
sections.html:
The county advertised a package it calls Project Zero. Bills for tax year 2026 were mailed and posted online after a September 22, 2026 announcement, and homestead property saw about 30 percent in total savings while other property saw about 20 percent. The relief came from four places:

  • The county cut its millage by 2 mills.
  • The school district cut its millage by 2 mills.
  • The county industrial development authority suspended its 2-mill levy.
  • Qualifying homesteads also receive a state grant.

All of that traces to the Project Camellia land sale. A Local Homeowners Incentive Adjustment Grant could let the county use available funds to erase county tax on qualifying homesteads in 2027, depending on the November 2026 referendum. Check effinghamtax.com for the outcome before you price a 2027 sale, since the bill a buyer inherits may look quite different from yours.

Real estate bills normally come due on November 20. Mobile homes follow a spring schedule, and the commissioner's page gives May 1. Late charges stack up in steps:

  • Interest of one percent per month starts the day after November 20.
  • Every 120 days adds 5 percent, with a cap at 20 percent overall.
  • Once taxes run past 90 days, the commissioner may record a fi. fa. with the court clerk, and credit bureaus can read it.
  • Levy on the property is the last resort, which the office says it would rather avoid.

Bills are addressed to the owner and never to a lender, so anyone with an escrow account should forward theirs to the servicer. Online e-check payment carries a $2 processing fee, noticeably lower than card fees.

You contest a value by appealing within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. There are two routes, the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, and superior court is open after either decision.

Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value, taken as of January 1 each year. The commissioner subtracts exemptions, then multiplies what remains by the millage rate, where one mill equals one dollar per $1,000 of assessed value.

The assessors accept appeals and waivers only by mail or hand delivery to 802 S. Laurel Street, North Administration Complex. If you hold a no-change notice and would rather skip the hearing, you can submit a waiver until a hearing date is set. A green postcard means an appraiser may visit your area within 60 days under state law. No response is needed.

The county publishes its own schedule, and a local amount overrides the state amount whenever it is larger. The main types:

  • Regular (S1): $4,000 for county tax and $2,000 for school tax.
  • Ages 62 to 64, income-tested (S3): $4,000 county and $10,000 school.
  • Age 65 and older (SC): $4,000 county and $12,000 school.
  • Age 65 and older, income-tested (S4): $6,000 county, $20,000 school, and $100 off the sanitation bill.
  • 100 percent disabled veteran (S5) and VA surviving spouse (SS): $101,754.

You qualify by owning and living in the home on January 1, and applications must land by April 1 for that year. The Tax Assessor's office takes them in person and online. Retitling a home to an LLC, renting out part of it, or claiming a second exemption elsewhere can end the exemption, and a double claim can draw a fine of two times the savings for up to three years.

sections.h2: What happens to your tax bill when you sell?
sections.html:
A sale ends the seller's exemption, since the county lists a sold property as grounds for removal, and the buyer applies for a new one. Before you list, ask the commissioner for a written balance covering every open year.

  • Clear old years from the proceeds so no lien rides along with the title.
  • Agree in the contract on who covers the 2026 bill.
  • Stop any lender escrow after payoff.

Years left unpaid can end in a public sale. The commissioner advertised a December 2026 tax sale for Tuesday, December 1, at 804 South Laurel Street between 10:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. Property goes for cash or certified funds, as is, with rights of redemption, and the buyer pays for title, transfer, advertising and recording. Parcels drop off the list when an owner pays, so the advertised list changes up to the sale.

A seller facing a sale date can choose a fast cash closing, which skips repairs, showings and lender delays. With a $276,000 median home value there is often real equity to protect, so act before the date, not after it.

faqs.q: When is the regular Effingham County bill due?
faqs.a: November 20 is the usual date. Interest begins the next day at one percent per month. Pay online, by phone at 470-531-3402, or at the commissioner's office.

faqs.q: Who accepts homestead applications in Effingham County?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessor's office does, and it also takes them online. File by April 1 or the exemption starts the following year. First-time owners should bring a copy of the warranty deed.

faqs.q: Is it too late to dispute a 2026 Effingham County value?
faqs.a: Probably. The window runs 45 days from the date printed on each notice, and for most owners that period has ended. File promptly after the next notice, and call 912-754-2125 for the right form.

faqs.q: Does a new Effingham County owner inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The county removes the exemption after a sale, and the new owner applies. Seniors and veterans must also reapply for the higher categories.

faqs.q: What happens at an Effingham County tax sale?
faqs.a: The ex-officio sheriff sells levied parcels at public outcry for cash or certified funds. Sales are as is and subject to redemption rights, and the buyer pays title, transfer, advertising and recording costs.
